key_insight: InclusionMed shows that medical AI rankings vary by healthcare role and capability, making overall scores insufficient for context-specific model selection.
clinical_relevance: Evaluating models against intended healthcare tasks may reveal performance differences that matter when considering their use in care settings.
method: Organized benchmarks across three healthcare roles and three AI capabilities.
Selected four public benchmarks from 388 candidates through structured audits and independent reproduction, then added a private diagnostic reasoning benchmark.
Evaluated frontier language models and aggregated results into overall, role-specific, and capability-specific InclusionMed Index scores.
evidence_signal: Index scores ranged from 17.5 to 49.1 out of 100, and all ten highest-ranked models scored higher on patient communication than on clinical decision-making in a task-tag analysis.
watch_item: The initial Atlas covers only three of nine role–capability cells, limiting conclusions about performance across diverse healthcare needs.
paper_title: InclusionMed: Benchmarking AI for Inclusive Healthcare
